web_title: 6. Multi-Year Financial Forensics, Balance Sheet Leverage & Daily-Reset Decay
book_title: Chapter 6: The Balance Sheet, the Depreciation Clock, and the Compounding Trap

epigraph.quote: Debt has a fixed maturity date and depreciation runs on a calendar; only equity—and especially leveraged equity derivatives—absorbs the full shock when cash flows arrive late.
epigraph.author: Credit & Derivatives Forensics

web_blocks.html: A forensic audit of Nebius Group N.V.'s financial statements from FY2024 through Q3 2026 reveals a business undergoing hyper-velocity top-line expansion financed by an equally dramatic transformation of its balance sheet [17][24][29]. Revenues leaped from $91.5 million in FY2024 to $529.8 million in FY2025 (+479% YoY). Hit $980.8 million in Q3 2026 alone (+571% YoY) [17][29]. Yet GAAP profitability and cash conversion remain heavily distorted by three structural factors: (1) aggressive GPU useful-life depreciation schedules, (2) upfront customer prepayments inflating operating cash flow, and (3) non-operating equity revaluations (such as the $598.9 million ClickHouse gain in FY2025) [24][30][31].

On the income statement, Nebius's single largest operating expense is Depreciation and Amortization (D&A). That totaled $404.0 million in FY2025. Representing 76.3% of full-year revenue [29]. Skeptical analysts have flagged that neoclouds extending GPU useful-life assumptions from 4 years to 5 or 6 years artificially flatter GAAP operating margins and understate the true economic replacement cycle of AI silicon, where NVIDIA's annual architecture cadence (Hopper to Blackwell to Rubin) can compress rental yields on older chips within 24 to 36 months [30]. Also. Meanwhile, Q3 2026 Adjusted EBITDA surged to $465.8 million, Adjusted EBITDA strips out D&A entirely. Ignoring the multi-billion-dollar hardware replacement treadmill [17][30].

web_blocks.takeaway: Nebius's cash balance rose to $7.43B in Q3 2026 not from free cash flow, but from issuing over $10.5B in convertible notes across 2025–2026 and drawing a $3.5B 364-day Citi credit facility—creating both interest drag and future equity dilution.

web_blocks.html: Balance-sheet forensics highlight the rapid shift from a debt-free post-Yandex cash shell in mid-2024 to a heavily leveraged capital structure by late 2026 [17][24]. In 2025, Nebius issued $4.84 billion in convertible bonds across four tranches. In August 2026, it issued another $5.75 billion in convertible notes. And in October 2026, it secured a $3.5 billion 364-day credit facility from Citigroup [17][24]. As of September 30, 2026, total carrying debt stood at $14.19 billion ($16.48 billion principal), driving Q3 2026 interest expense to $112.5 million alongside a $49.5 million induced conversion expense [17]. Meanwhile, issued and outstanding shares stood at 253.0 million at year-end 2025 (219.5 million Class A and 33.6 million Class B). This comes with substantial latent dilution embedded in the convertible bond stack and $83.2 million in annual share-based compensation [36][37].

When this levered, cash-burning balance sheet is wrapped inside NBIL, the compounding forensics turn doubly unforgiving. Every time NBIS announces a multi-billion-dollar convertible offering, a CapEx increase, or a colocation delay, the equity experiences sharp multi-day drawdowns followed by relief rallies. Inside NBIL, a -15% single-day drawdown becomes -30%. Recovering from a -30% drop requires a +42.9% gain, meaning NBIS must rise +21.4% in a single day. Or even more across multiple choppy sessions. Just for NBIL to break even. This asymmetric recovery math is the core forensic reason NBIL's 1-year return sits at -61.48% [1][5].

Equally important for forensic underwriting is the convertible-bond dilution overhang and refinancing wall embedded in NBIS's capital stack. Unlike simple bank term loans that merely consume interest, Nebius's $10.59 billion+ of convertible notes issued across 2025 and August 2026 act as deferred equity claims that cap upside participation when the stock rallies while remaining senior debt claims if AI compute demand cools [17][24]. Paired with the short-dated $3.5 billion 364-day Citigroup credit facility secured in October 2026, Nebius faces continuous capital-market refinancing dependency through 2027 [17]. For NBIL holders, this means the underlying stock is structurally exposed to periodic equity-linked supply and credit-spread repricing. Two catalysts that reliably inject high-volatility whipsaws into daily returns.

Finally, a complete forensic check must reconcile Nebius's non-operating asset cushion against its debt load. As of Q3 2026, Nebius held $7.43 billion in unrestricted cash (plus ~$1.2 billion in restricted cash), alongside its unconsolidated minority stakes in ClickHouse and Toloka AI and its consolidated ownership of Avride and TripleTen [4][15][17]. While those assets provide meaningful liquidity runway. Preventing any near-term solvency crunch. They are still outweighed by $16.48 billion in principal debt and a $27B–$45B annual CapEx trajectory [17]. Consequently, Nebius's net-debt position has shifted decisively negative. That leaves zero margin of safety if credit markets tighten.

For NBIL specifically, the forensic conclusion of Pass 1 is unambiguous: the ETF combines negative structural compounding at the derivative-wrapper level (1.41%–1.50% explicit fees, swap financing spreads. Quadratic daily volatility decay producing -61.48% 1Y performance) with an unproven, heavily levered, deeply FCF-negative underlying business [1][5][17]. Even if Nebius Group successfully executes its $12B–$13B FY2027 revenue ramp, the path between here and positive free cash flow runs through tens of billions of dollars in CapEx, convertible dilution. Quarterly execution volatility that mathematically erodes daily-reset 2x ETFs. Consequently, Pass 1 assigns NBIL a price-blind business quality verdict of FUNDAMENTAL_FAIL alongside a PASS_WITH_WATCH operational KPI rating for the underlying enterprise.

web_blocks.mechanism: Global Crossing raised tens of billions in convertible debt, high-yield bonds, and equity to lay global subsea fiber-optic cables ahead of projected internet traffic demand, booking upfront capacity swaps and prepayments while CapEx dwarfed operating cash flow.
web_blocks.outcome_numbers: Between 1999 and 2001, Global Crossing accumulated over $12.4B in debt against $3.8B in annual revenue before bandwidth pricing collapsed 70%–90% from industry overbuilding, culminating in a January 2002 Chapter 11 bankruptcy that wiped out 100% of common equity.
web_blocks.lesson_for_symbol: While Nebius's contracts are backed by investment-grade hyperscalers (Microsoft and Meta) rather than speculative dot-coms, the financial physics of debt-funded, multi-year infrastructure sprints remain hazardous: if GPU rental pricing compresses or financing windows shut before CapEx tapers, common equity—and 2x daily ETFs like NBIL—bear the first and sharpest loss.

web_blocks.title: Return on Invested Capital (ROIC) vs. Cost of Capital Verdict
paragraphs: Through FY2025 and 9M 2026, Nebius Group's GAAP ROIC remains negative on an unadjusted operating basis and deeply FCF-negative due to front-loaded CapEx. Until energized clusters convert backlog into sustained, post-depreciation operating cash flow that exceeds the cost of debt and equity dilution, economic value creation remains a future projection rather than a realized financial fact.

book_paragraphs: Now you and I arrive at the financial forensics, where stories meet spreadsheets and accounting choices meet the bank vault. Over the past two years, Nebius Group's top line has grown like wildfire: 91.5 million dollars in 2024, 529.8 million dollars in 2025, and 980.8 million dollars in the third quarter of 2026 alone. If you only read the revenue line, you would think you were looking at a classic software compounder.

Look one level deeper, and you see three forensic realities that explain why Nebius is nothing like a software compounder. Reality number one is the depreciation clock. In 2025, Nebius booked 404 million dollars of depreciation and amortization—more than seventy-six percent of its entire revenue. Critics rightly point out that spreading GPU depreciation over four, five, or six years flatters operating margins when NVIDIA releases a major new chip architecture every twelve to twenty-four months. When management points to Adjusted EBITDA of 465.8 million dollars in Q3 2026, remember that EBITDA conveniently erases the cost of replacing those chips.

Reality number two is cash conversion. Yes, Nebius generated 4.23 billion dollars of operating cash flow in the first nine months of 2026. But in Q3 2026 alone, it burned 7.30 billion dollars on capital expenditures, and operating cash flow actually swung negative by 273 million dollars as working capital shifted. The cash pile of 7.43 billion dollars on the balance sheet did not come from free cash flow—it came from capital markets.

book_subsections.title: From Debt-Free Shell to $16.48 Billion Principal Debt
paragraphs: That brings us to reality number three: the balance sheet transformation. When Nebius spun out of Yandex in 2024, it was essentially a debt-free cash shell. By September 30, 2026, carrying debt had surged to 14.19 billion dollars—16.48 billion in principal—driven by 4.84 billion dollars of convertible bonds in 2025, another 5.75 billion dollars of convertibles in August 2026, and a 3.5 billion dollar 364-day credit facility from Citi in October 2026. Quarterly interest expense reached 112.5 million dollars, and those convertible notes represent a massive overhang of potential share dilution on top of the 253 million shares already outstanding.

Think about what that capital structure does to your risk profile. Convertible bondholders enjoy debt protection on the downside and equity conversion on the upside—meaning they act like a silent ceiling on common shareholders when times are good, and a senior creditor when times are tight. Meanwhile, a 364-day credit facility means Nebius has to keep returning to Wall Street's refinancing window every single year to roll over billions of dollars while simultaneously executing a forty-to-forty-five-billion-dollar 2027 buildout.

Think back to the telecom fiber boom of 1999 to 2001—companies like Global Crossing that borrowed tens of billions to lay cables ahead of demand. Nebius has far stronger counterparties in Microsoft and Meta, but the leverage physics are unforgiving. And inside NBIL, every financing announcement or colocation delay triggers a two-times daily shock that compounds into permanent capital erosion—turning a minus 15 percent day into minus 30 percent, and forcing a painful uphill climb just to get back to even.

book_subsections.title: Why ROIC Remains Unproven and Cash Cushions Are Borrowed
paragraphs: When you put all the pieces together—the 404 million dollars of 2025 depreciation, the 16.48 billion dollars of principal debt by Q3 2026, the 83.2 million dollars of annual share-based compensation, and the minus 61.48 percent one-year return inside NBIL—a clear picture emerges. Nebius Group has built a 7.43 billion dollar cash cushion, plus valuable stakes in ClickHouse, Toloka, and Avride, which buys it real time to execute its hyperscaler contracts.

Yet a borrowed cash cushion is not the same thing as self-funding return on invested capital. Until Nebius proves that its GPU clusters earn enough post-depreciation operating cash flow to pay down debt and fund the next chip cycle internally, the underlying equity will remain a high-volatility capital-markets story—and NBIL will remain a daily-reset compounding trap for anyone who holds it past a single tactical swing.

Before we close Pass 1, remember why we do this entire six-chapter fundamental and forensic audit without looking at a single stock price or valuation multiple. By isolating the mechanics of the wrapper and the cash-flow physics of the business, you and I can see the truth with zero market-noise bias: NBIL fails fundamental compounding standards on both layers, and any future consideration of it must be strictly governed by tactical risk rules rather than long-term business ownership.

Take a moment to let that sink in. You do not need to know a single share price or valuation multiple to know that a daily-reset two-times swap ETF on a deeply free-cash-flow-negative, heavily indebted AI hardware builder is not a compounding vehicle. The math of daily rebalancing, the forty-to-forty-five-billion-dollar 2027 CapEx mountain, and the 16.48-billion-dollar principal debt stack tell the entire structural story on their own.

book_callouts.title: Mentor Check: Capital-Market Dependence Is the Ultimate Risk
book_callouts.quote: A company that must raise billions every few quarters to fund CapEx does not own its destiny; the credit and equity markets do.
book_callouts.text: When you and I finish the forensic audit of NBIL and NBIS, the verdict is crystal clear: NBIL fails fundamental compounding standards on both layers—as a decaying daily-reset derivative wrapper, and as an indirect claim on a deeply FCF-negative, heavily leveraged hardware buildout.
